chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hamza ibn Hamran, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
Indeed, the one who answers in all he is asked, is surely insane.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be 'insane' in the context of answering questions in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the term 'insane' (*majnun*) metaphorically to warn against the folly of indiscriminate speech, a key principle in Shia *adab* of knowledge. This teaching emphasizes that true wisdom lies in discerning when to speak and when to remain silent, preventing the dilution of one's authority and insight through excessive or unnecessary disclosure.
